title: MEG extends dip amid weak textile demand
summary:
Asian MEG prices continued correcting through May 2026 as weak polyester, textile and PET resin demand reduced buying activity across China, India and Southeast Asia.
Competitive imported cargoes widened pressure on Chinese domestic producers, while textile mills adopted cautious hand-to-mouth purchasing amid weak export orders and uncertainty linked to US-Iran geopolitical tensions.

title: Sri Lanka gets $695 mn IMF tranche as economic risks rise
summary:
The Middle East war has significantly worsened Sri Lanka’s economic outlook and tilted risks to the downside, with 2026 growth projected to slow down to 3 per cent, the IMF has said. 
Its executive board has completed the combined fifth and sixth reviews of the Extended Fund Facility for the country. 
This provided the country with immediate access to $695 million to support economic policies and reforms.

title: US team to visit India from June 1-4 to finalise interim trade pact
summary:
A US team will visit India from June 1 to 4 to finalise the details of the bilateral interim agreement and take forward talks on a broader bilateral trade agreement (BTA), the Indian Ministry of Commerce announced yesterday. 
This will be the second in-person meeting between the two sides since February 2026. 
India’s chief negotiator Darpan Jain had the last in-person meeting in Washington DC in April.

title: US, Mexico launch USMCA review talks for stronger regional trade
summary:
The United States and Mexico will hold three bilateral negotiating rounds under the first Joint Review of the USMCA between May and July 2026.
Talks will focus on economic security, industrial rules of origin, agriculture and fair competition, with both countries aiming to strengthen regional trade benefits for manufacturers, workers and SMEs.

title: ICE cotton extends decline on weak crude, better US weather
summary:
ICE cotton futures extended losses to fresh one-and-a-half-month lows as falling crude oil prices, improved US weather forecasts and rising certified stocks pressured sentiment.
Better rainfall prospects in West Texas and faster US planting progress reinforced expectations of stable supplies, while weaker crude reduced cotton’s competitiveness against cheaper polyester fibre.

title: Italian economy projected to continue to grow at modest pace: IMF
summary:
Economic activity in Italy faces an increasingly challenging near‑term outlook, with the economy projected to grow at a modest pace, weighed down by external headwinds and structural challenges, the IMF said. 
Medium‑term growth prospects are subdued, constrained by weak productivity growth and population aging. 
Uncertainty around the outlook is high, as downside risks to growth accumulate, it noted.

title: Italy’s industrial turnover index up 2% MoM in value in March
summary:
Italy’s seasonally-adjusted industrial turnover index increased by an estimated 2 per cent month on month (MoM) in value and 0.7 per cent MoM in volume in March this year. 
In Q1 2026, the index rose by 1.3 per cent quarter on quarter (QoQ) and decreased by 0.5 per cent QoQ in volume. 
The calendar-adjusted industry turnover index rose by 4.4 per cent YoY in value and 2 per cent YoY in volume in March.

title: Eurozone financial stability vulnerabilities elevated: ECB
summary:
The outlook for euro area financial stability is being shaped by geo-economic stress and energy supply disruptions, with the severity and duration of the fallout still uncertain, the European Central Bank said. 
Fiscal expansion in a challenging geo-economic environment could strain public finances further in some highly indebted euro area countries and lead to a repricing of sovereign risk.

title: Australia’s Q1 cotton exports rise 16% despite price pressure
summary:
Australia’s cotton exports rose 16 per cent year-on-year to $210.3 million in Q1 2026, driven by a sharp increase in shipments to China, which regained its position as the top buyer.
However, lower average export prices reflected softer global cotton markets.
Exports to Bangladesh and India declined, highlighting changing sourcing patterns and shifting trade competitiveness.

title: Australia’s consumer inflation eases to 4.2% in April 2026
summary:
Australia’s CPI inflation eased to 4.2 per cent YoY in April 2026 from 4.6 per cent in March, mainly due to slower growth in goods prices and lower automotive fuel inflation, according to ABS. 
However, trimmed mean inflation edged up to 3.4 per cent. 
Clothing and footwear prices rose strongly, while transport costs declined monthly but remained elevated annually.

title: Bangladesh denim’s next advantage is the supply chain behind jeans
summary:
Bangladesh’s denim strength is shifting from low-cost garment assembly towards full value-chain control.
TexPro data shows trousers, cotton apparel and woven exports remain central to the country’s apparel economy.
However, energy shortages, imported fabric dependence and fibre-traceability demands are pushing suppliers towards deeper vertical integration.

title: Premium fashion’s scale trap
summary:
Australian and European premium apparel exporters are facing the same challenge: rising compliance, traceability and trade costs without the export scale needed to absorb them.
Australia lacks manufacturing depth and remains heavily import dependent, while Europe struggles to convert its large apparel base into globally competitive export growth.

title: China’s quiet apparel corridor to Russia is no side route anymore
summary:
China is building a more direct and formalised apparel supply route into Russia through factory clusters, rail logistics and Russia-specific product development.
Rising imports and faster rail-linked replenishment are helping Chinese suppliers gain share in Russia’s market.
However, weaker consumer spending and tighter compliance rules could create inventory and risks for smaller importers.

title: Price check: What 38% of Europeans want from green fashion
summary:
European consumers increasingly expect brands and governments to make sustainable fashion more affordable, transparent and accessible.
Regulations such as DPP and Extended Producer Responsibility EPR are pushing companies towards greater accountability.
However, high prices, greenwashing concerns and limited consumer awareness continue to slow wider adoption of sustainable fashion.

title: Japan’s apparel imports rebound to $2.1 bn in April 2026
summary:
Japan’s apparel imports rebounded in April 2026 after declining in March, reaching around $2.17 billion and accounting for 3.4 per cent of total imports.
Textile yarn and fabric imports and exports also posted gains, while textile machinery exports rose strongly.
Over recent fiscal years, Japan has maintained relatively steady growth in apparel imports and machinery exports.

title: India’s Sahu International Attire to build RMG unit in UP’s YEIDA belt
summary:
Sahu International Attire will invest ₹700 million in a garment manufacturing facility in the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority region of Uttar Pradesh (UP) state that is expected to create 2,000 jobs. 
The company is among 17 firms that received allotment letters by UP chief minister Yogi Adityanath for setting up projects covering several sectors, including solar energy and green energy.

title: Hong Kong apparel imports edge down in Q1 2026
summary:
Hong Kong’s apparel imports declined slightly to $1.431 billion in January-March 2026 amid softer sourcing activity.
China remained the largest supplier despite a marginal fall in market share, while Vietnam, France and Japan expanded their presence.
The trading hub continued to maintain its role as an independent customs territory and global re-export centre.

title: Coats & JACK launch integrated solution for Chinese apparel SMEs
summary:
Coats Group PLC & JACK Technology Co Ltd have signed a strategic cooperation agreement to accelerate innovation for China’s growing apparel SME sector. 
The partnership combines Coats’ high-performance thread, digital software and technical support with JACK’s intelligent sewing equipment to help manufacturers improve shop-floor efficiency, productivity and inventory management.

title: Sri Lanka apparel exports decline amid weaker global demand: JAAF
summary:
Sri Lanka’s apparel exports fell 4.72 per cent year-on-year to $328.15 million in April 2026 due to weaker demand from the UK, EU, and US markets, according to JAAF.
Exports to other destinations rose 12.61 per cent, highlighting diversification opportunities.
JAAF said improving competitiveness and policy support will be crucial for long-term sector growth.

title: US’ Deckers sees continued growth momentum for HOKA and UGG in FY26
summary:
Deckers Brands has reported record FY26 revenue of $5.47 billion, up 9.8 per cent YoY, with diluted EPS rising 11 per cent to $7.02, driven by strong HOKA and UGG sales. 
Fourth-quarter revenue increased 9.6 per cent to $1.12 billion. 
The company forecast high-single-digit sales growth for FY27 and expanded its share repurchase authorisation to approximately $5 billion.
